checkpoints.description: [1/2] Ship a chaos fuzz harness and prove the engine survives random play

impact_assessment.why: all recent verification followed the AI captain's deliberate route; random legal action sequences (blocking encounters, odd trades, dismissals) had never been exercised, so unhandled state combinations were untested
impact_assessment.benefits: a reusable tool turns random play into a repeatable invariant check with reproducible seed/step reporting and Why/Fix exit guidance
impact_assessment.risks: contract: none, a new developer tool plus fast unit tests; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: five fast tests pin the checker against a synthetic bad state covering all twelve rule classes, plus the clean case, dedup, priority and a small seeded run

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Loading keeps an emptied crew, weapon rack or inbox empty

impact_assessment.benefits: deliberate player choices survive a reload, and the fuzz now field-compares 400 arbitrary save/load round trips
impact_assessment.risks: contract: legacy backfill is gated on the pre-RNG-checkpoint marker; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Press the structural systems with the chaos fuzz

impact_assessment.why: the harness only sampled flight, trade, encounters and crew, leaving power routing, reactor modes, outposts, escorts, ship mods, upgrades, research, contracts and depots untouched by random play
impact_assessment.benefits: every stateful ship-building system now sees random input and its refusals, and reactor bounds join the invariant checks
impact_assessment.risks: contract: tool-only, no production route changes; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: prerequisites are left to the engine's refusals, and refusal/success counts partition the actions

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Core heat follows the fitted capacity and survives a save exactly

impact_assessment.why: the save interleaving found heat rounded on save (0.005 drift) and clamped to the base max_heat on load, silently cooling a core that legitimately sat above the base cap, while removing a thermal mod left the core above its new capacity
impact_assessment.benefits: thermal capacity is respected everywhere, saves are lossless, and a reload no longer rewrites the reactor
impact_assessment.risks: contract: ReactorState serialization now keeps exact floats and load-time clamping is removed; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: live states obey the fitted capacity because every equipment change clamps
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests for capacity change, 120-heat save round trip, clamp after removal, negative-heat repair and integrity clamp, plus the 20-seed save-interleaved fuzz

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Make the shadow backup an atomic rename instead of a second copy

impact_assessment.why: the server saves after every mutation; a 485 KB save cost 36.9 ms and the .bak copy+fsync alone cost 17.6 ms, more than writing the new payload (6.6 ms), because the previous file is already durable
impact_assessment.benefits: save latency halves without weakening crash safety: the renamed backup is the previous durable state and load already falls back to it
impact_assessment.risks: contract: save format and load fallback unchanged; dependency: none; concurrency: the existing write lock still serializes saves; state: a power loss between rename and install recovers the previous save from .bak
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests for the no-copy path, backup content, first-save absence, failed-install recovery and named slots, plus the save-interleaved fuzz and benchmark campaigns

checkpoints.description: [1/2] Action responses omit the static catalogs

impact_assessment.why: every action response carried 193 KB, 57 KB of it code-constant catalogs the headless captain re-downloaded and rebuilt on ~1000 steps, although the server already supports stripping them behind X-VoidFarer-Catalogs
impact_assessment.benefits: each step moves 56 KB less JSON and skips the static snapshot build, while the five policies that read catalogs keep working through a one-time cache
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the header constant moves to engine.py as the single definition; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: the captain caches immutable build constants, so staleness is impossible within a session
impact_assessment.mitigation: six new tests pin the cache seeding, header on every action, full initial fetch, rehydration, fresh-value precedence and empty-snapshot guard; gate and both benchmark campaigns re-measured
